facts.statement: Sauroplites was a herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Sauroplites (meaning "saurian hoplite") is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in 1930 by Swedish paleontologist Anders Birger Bohlin near Tebch in Inner Mongolia during Sven Hedin's expeditions.
facts.quote: In 1930, the Swedish paleontologist Anders Birger Bohlin during the Swedish-Chinese expeditions of Sven Hedin discovered an ankylosaurian fossil near Tebch in Inner Mongolia.

facts.statement: The type species Sauroplites scutiger was formally named and described by Bohlin in 1953.
facts.quote: The type species Sauroplites scutiger was named and described by Bohlin in 1953.

facts.statement: The generic name Sauroplites means "saurian hoplite" and is derived from Greek words for lizard and armed foot soldier.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek sauros or saura, "lizard", and hoplites, "hoplite, armed foot soldier".

facts.statement: The specific name scutiger means "shield bearer" in Neo-Latin, referring to the animal's body armor.
facts.quote: The specific name is Neo-Latin for "shield bearer", in reference to the body armour.

facts.statement: Sauroplites was often considered a nomen dubium and some researchers believed it might actually belong to the genus Shamosaurus.
facts.quote: Sauroplites was later often considered a nomen dubium because it is based on fragmentary material. Some believed it might actually be a specimen of another ankylosaur, Shamosaurus.

facts.statement: The original specimens are lost and lack an inventory number, but casts exist at the American Museum of Natural History as specimen AMNH 2074.
facts.quote: The specimens were not given an inventory number and are today lost, though some casts are present in the American Museum of Natural History as specimen AMNH 2074.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Zhidan Group, dating from the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: They were found in a layer of the Zhidan Group, probably dating from the Barremian to Aptian stages.

facts.statement: Oval osteoderms with an asymmetric low keel covered the back and could reach a length of up to forty centimeters.
facts.quote: More to the front oval osteoderms, with an asymmetric low keel, cover the back, with a length of up to forty centimetres.

facts.statement: Osteoderms thirty centimeters long covered the sides of the animal.
facts.quote: Thirty centimetre osteoderms cover the sides.

facts.statement: Sauroplites is estimated to have been around six meters long.
facts.quote: Se estima que el sauroplite media alrededor de 6 metros de largo.

facts.statement: While Bohlin originally placed Sauroplites in Ankylosauridae, a 2014 cladistic analysis by Arbour recovered it as a member of Nodosauridae based on its unique sacral shield.
facts.quote: Bohlin placed Sauroplites in the Ankylosauridae. However, Arbour (2014) considered it possible that it was a member of the Nodosauridae in view of the possession of a sacral shield consisting of fused rosettes which is unknown with unequivocal ankylosaurids, even though nodosaurid remains from Asia are rare and contentious. In a cladistic analysis she performed, Sauroplites was recovered as a nodosaurid.

facts.statement: Sauroplites lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 112 million years ago during the Aptian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 125 a 112 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in Gansu province, China.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la provincia de Gansu, China.

facts.statement: The time range for Sauroplites is estimated to be between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests the carcass was deposited on its back, with the body armor largely articulated while other bones were eroded away.
facts.quote: The carcass had been deposited on its back and the bones had been eroded away, apart from some ribs and perhaps a piece of an ischium, leaving parts of the body armour in a largely articulated position.

rejected.quote: However, in 2014 Victoria Megan Arbour discovered a clear unique trait, autapomorphy: the sacral or pelvic shield shows rosettes with a large central osteoderm surrounded by a single ring of smaller scutes.
